quote: Vidisha has a hoary past, with a rich archaeology and history. The archaeological wealth scattered all over the District, speaks of the glory that was Vidisha. It has been referred to in the Epics, the Puranas and in the Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical literature. The religious tolerance of the age is reflected here in the numerous Brahmanical, Buddhist and Jain remains, which coexisted. The Heliodoros Pillar or the Garuddhwaja at Besnagar, that was ancient Vidisha of the Sunga period, the Udayagiri caves of the Gupta period, the magnificent temples at Gyaraspur, Udayapur and Badoh symbolise the rich cultural heritage of this District.

The historicity of the ancient city of Besnagar, three kilometres from modern Vidisha and identified with ancient Vidisha, goes back to some centuries before the birth of Christ. quote: Actually Pushyamitra performed not one, but two Asvamedha sacrifices to herald the victory of Brahmanism over the Buddhist faith.\(^{2}\) One of the Asvamedha sacrifices was probably performed at Vidisha itself, as evidenced by the recent excavations\(^{3}\). Pushyamitra ruled for about 36 years (187-151 B.C.) and at the end of an eventful life left for his son Agnimitra a vast territory, including the cities of Pataliputra, Ayodhya, Vidisha and probably Jalandhar and Sakala.\(^{4}\) There is a reference in the Malavikagnimitram to the newly formed independent kingdom in the region of Vidarbha.

He is mentioned therein as having come as the ambassador of the Indo-Greek King Antialcidas of Taxila to the court of King Bhagabhadra. This Bhagabhadra is generally identified with the fifth Shunga king Bhandaka of the later Shungas who are supposed to have made Vidisha their capital.

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
विदिशा उदयपुर की तुलना में बड़ा और अधिक प्राचीन शहर था, जिसका ज्ञात इतिहास ही मौर्ष्य तक तो बड़े आराम से ले जाता है। मौर्ष्य साम्राज्य में अशोक सम्राट बनने के पहले उज्जैन में रहे थे। विदिशा के पास सांची के स्तूप तभी बनना शुरू हुए थे। कालिदास के मेघदूत विदिशा की आकाशीय यात्रा करते हुए दिखाई दिए हैं। बीच में गुप्त काल गुजरा, जिसके प्रमाण इस इलाके में जगह-जगह बिखरे हुए हैं।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Vidisha was a bigger and more ancient city than Udaipur, whose known history goes back easily to the Mauryas. Ashoka lived in Ujjain before becoming emperor. The Sanchi stupas near Vidisha began to be built then. Kalidasa's clouds travel through Vidisha in the Meghaduta. Then came the Gupta period, whose evidence is scattered around the region.
note: Vidisha larger and older than Udaypur, known history reaching Mauryas; Sanchi stupas, Kalidasa's Meghaduta and Gupta remains.

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
यह एक ऐसे शहर की यादगार यात्रा थी, जहां दो हज़ार साल पहले एक यूनानी राजदूत आया था। उसने विदिशा आकर यहां के समाज और रीति-रिवाजों के असर में वैष्णव धर्म स्वीकार करने का निर्णय ले लिया था। वह इतिहास में दर्ज विदिशा के लिए गर्व करने लायक एक अमर प्रसंग है, जिसकी याद बेतवा नदी के किनारे पत्थर के एक स्तंभ में दर्ज है। वह स्तंभ खामबाबा के नाम से प्रसिद्ध है, जो कभी एक मंदिर के सामने गढ़ स्तंभ की शक्ल में स्थापित किया गया होगा। आज मंदिर का नामोनिशान बाकी नहीं है। लेकिन हेलिओडोरस का वह लेख आज भी उस स्तंभ पर पढ़ा जा सकता है।
*Gloss [my translation]:* It was a memorable visit to a city where two thousand years ago a Greek ambassador came. Moved by the society and customs, he decided to accept Vaishnavism. It is an immortal episode recorded on a stone pillar on the Betwa, famed as Khambaba, once a garuda pillar before a temple. No trace of the temple remains, but Heliodorus's inscription can still be read on the pillar.
note: Heliodorus's visit to Vidisha and conversion to Vaishnavism, recorded on the Khambaba pillar by the Betwa.

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
जब वह पहली बार यहां आया था तब मगध सम्राट अशोक और पुण्यमित्र शुंग के किस्से बहुत ताजे थे। सांची में स्तूपों का निर्माण जारी था। महेंद्र और संघमित्रा श्रीलंका प्रस्थान के पहले अपनी माता से मिलने आए थे। शुंगों की यज्ञवेदियों के धुएं की सुगंध हवाओं को ताजादम बनाए हुए थे।
*Gloss [my translation]:* When he first came, the stories of Magadha's Emperor Ashoka and Pushyamitra Shunga were very fresh. Stupas were still being built at Sanchi. note: Imagined account of Heliodorus's time: Ashoka and Pushyamitra Shunga stories fresh, Sanchi stupas under construction, Mahendra and Sanghamitra visiting their mother.

book_title: कथा उदयपुर (Jagta Hua Kasba) — Hindi original
quote:
वह भी विदिशा को दिल दे बैठा। इतना कि उसने अपना धर्म ही बदल लिया। इसकी विधिवत घोषणा एक बड़े स्तंभ पर अंकित करा दी थी ताकि इतिहास को भलीभांति पता रहे।
*Gloss [my translation]:* He gave his heart to Vidisha so much that he changed his religion. He had it formally announced inscribed on a large pillar so that history would know it well.

note: Patari, about 15 km from Udaypur and midway between them on Google Maps, has ruins suggesting a developed town in Mauryan and Gupta times.

Bhāillasvāmippura (l. 9) is the ancient city of Vidishā (Bhilsā), which was formerly the capital of the Akara-janapada, roughly corresponding to east Mālava. The name Bhillasvāmin (Bhāillasāmin) was originally of an image of the Sun deity worshipped in a temple at that place which subsequently became famous under the deity's name, as we also know from Albērūnī (c. 1030 A.C.) who tells us that “the name of the town is identical with that of the idol worshipped there”. Rising above the bold podium mouldings, the wall consists of ornate offsets alternating with plain angular wall surface, the whole surmounted by the shikhara. The major offsets are decorated with niches which are surmounted by tall pediments and contain images of Ganesha, Karttikeya, Uma and the eight Regents of quarters, which represent fine specimens of the Pratihara art. - यह वही महामार्ग था जिससे होकर ‘द्राविड़ ऊपजी’ भक्तिधारा ने उत्तर भारत में एक से बढ़ कर एक दीपस्तम्भ जगमगा दिए थे। ऐसा ही एक जागृत दीपस्तम्भ था उदयपुर का उदयेश्वर महादेव देवालय।
*Gloss [my translation]:* That path joining Uttarapatha to Dakshinapatha was not merely a highway of transport but a great path of devotion, on which various dynasties such as Chera, Chola, Pandya, Chalukya and Rashtrakuta built countless temple-towns and cities to keep Indian eternal culture unbroken. author: Adam Hardy
context: … Rock-Cut Architecture Other than the ruins of the Indus Valley civilisation and various megaliths, the earliest brick or stone architecture surviving in the subcontinent comprises the free-standing columns erected by the Mauryas, most famously by Ashoka (c 268–233 BC), and the Buddhist stupas, monasteries and chaitya halls which grew up from that time onwards along the trade routes of the ancient empires. Ashoka himself almost certainly built stupas, made of brick. With its solid dome and cosmic axis, the stupa, which has its origins in burial mounds, is the most characteristic sacred monument of Buddhism. One of its multiple associations is the Buddha's achievement of Nirvana on leaving this world. Early stupas were raised to encase relics of the Buddha or of a disciple or a saint, and thus radiated miraculous power.\(^{1}\) The great stupas of peninsular India, originally surrounded by thriving monastic complexes, belong to the period between the 2nd century BC and the 3rd century AD (7.1). 7.1 The Great Stupa (Stupa 1), Sanchi (MP), c 1st century BC, probably built over an earlier structure, which would have encased a sacred relic. book_title: The Cultural Heritage of Madhya Bharat — Patil, D. R.
